summary: Adds a novel top-level command `garmin-pp-cli history` (internal/cli/garmin_sync.go, internal/cli/garmin_window.go) plus its store support (internal/store/garmin_series.go), registered beside the generated sync at internal/cli/root.go with a single AddCommand line. Nothing in the generated sync.go, store.go, or any generated command file was edited. The generated `sync` keeps owning the resources the profiler could genuinely enumerate; `history` owns the calendar walk the press cannot express. Why the press cannot express it: Garmin has no since-based list endpoint for its daily statistics. Every daily series is either a date-RANGE endpoint whose path IS the range (/usersummary-service/stats/steps/daily/{start}/{end}) or a per-DATE endpoint answering for exactly one day. The profiler marks an endpoint syncable only when its path has no parameters (profiler.go:586-589,657), unresolved {placeholders} are skipped with a sync_warning (sync.go.tmpl:58-65), and the only temporal sync flag is --dates for a query parameter literally named dates|date_range|daterange (profiler.go:3042). So the windowed walk, its per-series calendar state, and its caller-keyed writes are all novel. FIRST APPLIED 2026-09-07 (N131.4); EXTENDED 2026-09-13 (N131.5.1) with three more series and a fifth series kind; DEPTH MODEL REPLACED 2026-09-13 (N131.5.2, decisions D12 and D15). WHAT THE COMMAND DOES: fifteen series across five kinds (steps, sleep_stats, sleep_score, max_metrics, intensity_minutes, resting_hr as date-ranged; daily_summary, sleep_detail, daily_hr, training_readiness as per-day; activities as an offset-paged feed; activity_hr_zones, activity_detail and activity_splits as per-activity fan-outs over the stored activity ids; hr_zone_config as a single-document series -- one request for the account's heart-rate zone configuration, stored under the fixed id "current" and replaced in place on every run, because it is the current setting rather than a dated observation). DEPTH AND ORDER (N131.5.2): every series walks OLDEST DAY FIRST and keeps ONE bookmark, last_complete_day, so an interrupted run resumes at bookmark + 1. A state row means 'filled from earliest_day through last_complete_day'. A run has at most two legs: an EXTENSION leg, taken only when this run asks for a floor below earliest_day, which walks from that floor up to earliest_day - 1 and stamps the new floor only on completion (an interrupted extension simply restarts from the floor next run -- idempotent upserts, and no gap nothing would return to); and a FORWARD leg from last_complete_day + 1 to today, checkpointed after every window, day or page. Depth has exactly one control, --since: `all` fills from each series' own floor, a date fills from there, and nothing at all keeps the depth the archive already has and only catches up to today. A --since above the stored floor is accepted, changes nothing below it and says so once on stderr. FLOORS: the windowed series start at garminHistoryFloor = 2007-01-01, which is where Garmin Connect starts -- no discovery call and no assumption about when the account holder first wore something (a first-activity floor is false for a watch-only account and for wellness recorded before the first activity, and none of Garmin's three account documents carries a creation date); the activity feed asks Garmin directly in one request (sortOrder=asc&limit=1, probed live 2026-09-13 on both homes: 2012-03-11 and 2011-10-29) and then pages ascending within a date range; the per-day series walk SIGNAL DAYS only. The backward walk, the empty-window ceiling, frontier_day and the stop reasons window_denied_stop / empty_window_ceiling / never_returned_data are all retired, and --days, --backfill and --empty-window-ceiling are DELETED flags, not hidden aliases. WINDOW SIZES ARE PER SERIES AND WERE MEASURED, NOT ASSUMED (live A/B, 2026-09-07, populated account): steps, sleep_stats and sleep_score return HTTP 400 for a 364-day range and 200 for 28 days, so they are pinned at Garmin's 28-day cap; resting_hr (/userstats-service/wellness/daily/{displayName}?metricId=60) returned 364 rows for a 364-day range, max_metrics returned 79 sparse rows across a year, and intensity_minutes returned 53 weekly rows -- all three are set to 364, which is 13x fewer requests than a blanket 28 would cost. STATE: a novel garmin_series_state table holds last_complete_day, earliest_day, stop_reason, total_rows and walk_version per series, and is checkpointed after EVERY window so a run killed mid-walk resumes rather than re-walking. frontier_day and empty_windows remain as columns so an existing archive still loads, and nothing reads them. walk_version (added by ALTER TABLE at open, idempotent) is why the old state cannot mislead the new walk: a row below store.GarminWalkVersion was written by the retired backward walk, whose last_complete_day was the top of a range walked downwards rather than the top of a contiguous fill, so it is READ AS UNFILLED and rewritten at the current version on the first save. total_rows is now RECOUNTED from the archive at the end of every series rather than accumulated, because this walk deliberately re-requests the feed's boundary day and a refresh window of days on every run. It lives in its own table rather than in sync_state because earliest_day costs a multi-year re-walk to rebuild and must survive a generated cursor clear (regression-tested). Each series' progress is also mirrored into the generated sync_state so doctor, tail and generated incremental readers still see it. Today is never bookmarked complete -- the day is still accruing -- though today's partial row is stored. SIGNAL DAYS (N131.5.2): a per-day request costs one call and up to 88 KB, so a per-day series asks only for days the archive already shows a reading for -- a row in steps, resting_hr, sleep_stats, sleep_score or max_metrics, or the start day of a stored activity. intensity_minutes is excluded because it answers weekly with null-valued rows back to 2007 on both reference accounts, so its days are a property of the endpoint rather than evidence anybody wore anything. On the Kavita archive the union covers every archived per-day row and every calendar day since 2020-07-06; on the sparse owner archive it is about 134 days instead of 1 908. A day that was requested and came back empty sits inside the filled range and is never requested again, with one exception: the newest seven complete signal days are re-requested every run, because a day can be fetched before the device that recorded it has finished uploading. HONESTY RULE, RE-ORIENTED FOR OLDEST-FIRST: an HTTP 403 is read as a window before the account existed only while the series has stored no row AND this run has already had one request answered 200; otherwise it counts toward the consecutive-failure wall and the bookmark does not move. A series whose every requested window was refused is not marked complete (stop_reason=all_windows_refused, bookmark unchanged) -- the failure prevented is a dead or blocked token turning a first fill into a silent 'complete, 0 rows'. PACING AND 429: 300 ms between calls (the interval a 94-window live backfill walked at without a single 429, N131 section 9.2) and a hard fail-fast on the first 429 -- the remaining series are not attempted and the command exits 7. Note the generated client still makes up to 3 Retry-After-respecting attempts on the call that 429s (client.go:1066,1253-1289); that ceiling is not settable without a verified platform session (client.go:83-95), so the fail-fast is at the walker. EVENTS: sync_start, sync_progress, sync_warning, sync_anomaly and sync_summary, the same vocabulary the generated sync emits, on stderr under a machine format and stdout otherwise. The emitter is nil-safe, ignores write errors and marshals every dynamic field, so telemetry can never break the walk it observes. CLOSING DOCUMENT (2026-09-18): under a machine format the run also prints ONE JSON document on stdout when the walk ends -- total_records, resources, success, warned, errored, duration_ms -- through printJSONFiltered, the same helper and the same six keys the generated sync prints (internal/cli/sync.go, the printJSONFiltered call after its exit-code policy), so --select and --compact act on it exactly as they do there. It is printed AFTER the exit-code checks, matching sync.go's own order: a run that returns an error -- --strict with a failed series, a 429 fail-fast, the consecutive-failure wall -- prints its events and no document, so a caller never reads a summary document from a walk that did not finish. Events stay on stderr under a machine format; human mode, --status and --dry-run are unchanged. Before this the machine-mode stdout of `history` was empty, which contradicted the Agent Mode contract both README and SKILL render: `--json` -- one JSON document on stdout, sync progress events go to stderr. STORE: UpsertKeyedBatch takes the row id from the caller rather than extracting it from the payload -- Garmin's daily rows are keyed by calendarDate and its hrTimeInZones payload is a bare array with no id at all -- and otherwise follows the generated write path exactly (merge-preserving generic row, FTS, typed-table projection under a per-row savepoint). ACTIVITY PAGING: the feed is paged with `start`, not `offset`. Verified live 2026-09-07: start=5 returns the sixth-newest activity onward, offset=5 returns the same page as start=0. A future regen must keep this; see the open finding on the generated sync below. THREE MECHANISMS THE LIVE RUN ADDED, each because the run exposed the gap: (1) the activity feed's depth was clamped to a --days horizon on a first run, because an unclamped first `history --days 56` paged the whole feed back to 2011-10-29 (3 246 activities, 33 pages) while every other series covered 56 days -- RETIRED by N131.5.2, which gives the feed the same floor-and-bookmark model as every other series; (2) a series that completes a run having never stored a single row emits sync_warning reason series_returned_no_rows, because training_readiness returned an empty list for all 56 days and said nothing, leaving an empty table that reads like a settled fact when it is an unproven zero; (3) a consecutive-failure breaker (--max-consecutive-failures, default 10) ends the run when that many calls fail in a row, because a second live run whose credential had gone stale answered HTTP 403 to all 39 of its requests and emitted 39 separate warnings for one condition before finishing. Neither 403 nor 401 carries a Retry-After or a rate-limit error type, so nothing in the per-call error path distinguishes a refused request from a finished client; a whole run failing is a different fact from a request failing and is now reported once and acted on immediately. ARCHIVE NAME: `history` and `insights` resolve the archive through garminArchivePath (internal/cli/garmin_sync.go), not through the generated defaultDBPath, and the file is always `<data>/data.db` -- the name N131 section 3 gives it. The generated resolver (internal/cli/helpers.go defaultDBPathInDir) names the archive `data-<sha256(auth header)[:12]>.db`, scoping it to the credential in use; Garmin's DI chain rotates its refresh token on every refresh and its access token roughly daily, so under a daily sync that name changes and every rotation orphans the previous file, leaving `history` to re-walk years of history into a new one. Nothing about a Garmin home needs credential scoping: N131 section 2 Q3 binds one account to one home, so the home already is the isolation boundary. garminArchivePath does not merely return a different path, because the generated `sync`, `analytics` and `search` must not end up on a different file: it makes the unscoped file EXIST. The generated branch order is scoped-exists first, then unscoped-exists, so the fix works precisely because the migration leaves no scoped file behind. Fresh home: an empty 0600 data.db is created (a zero-byte file is a valid empty SQLite database). One scoped archive and no data.db: it is renamed, once, with a notice on stderr. Deviation from a single atomic rename, and the reason: the store opens WAL, so a -wal/-shm pair can sit beside the archive and renaming the main file alone would strand its committed transactions; the store is opened and closed first to checkpoint the WAL back in, then one rename carries everything, and any sidecar SQLite still leaves behind is renamed alongside rather than deleted. Both names present: nothing is renamed (a rename would overwrite), the novel commands take data.db and a warning names the consequence -- the generated commands prefer the scoped file, so they are writing a different archive. Two or more scoped archives and no data.db: renaming either would discard the other, so an empty data.db is started and every candidate is named. The migration matches only the generated name shape (data- plus exactly 12 hex characters plus .db), so it globs rather than recomputing the current hash -- the orphaned file on disk is scoped to a PREVIOUS credential. COST REPORTING (N131.5.2): after the cheap series finish and before the first fan-out or per-day call, the run prints one line -- "About R requests, about T, up to S MB -- after which the archive covers <day> to today." (the date is where the archive ENDS UP, not where the run starts; corrected in the N131.5.2 fix round, finding B1) -- computed from the archive alone by internal/cli/garmin_plan.go: outstanding fan-out ids, outstanding signal days, this archive's own mean row size once a series holds 30 rows and a measured constant before that (detail 3 327 B, splits 2 666 B, zones 358 B, daily_summary 2 666 B, daily_hr 12 977 B, sleep_detail 88 340 B; measured 2026-09-13 over the Kavita archive), and requests x (pacing delay + 130 ms observed latency). In human mode it goes to stderr; under --json it is the one event name outside the generated sync vocabulary, sync_estimate. `history --status` prints the same state as a table or --json (rows, filled from, complete through, outstanding, stopped because), and `--dry-run` prints the plan plus the estimate. Neither builds a client, so 'makes no request' is a property of the code path rather than a promise about it. FLAG SURFACE (decision D12): --since and --status are the only visible flags; --series, --delay, --page-size, --max-pages, --max-dependents (now defaulting to 0, no cap), --max-consecutive-failures, --strict and --db stay functional but hidden, because each of them is an implementation detail leaking into a choice the caller should not have to make. FAN-OUTS ARE BOUNDED BY THE RUN'S FLOOR (N131.5.3, decision D16): activity_detail, activity_splits and activity_hr_zones fetch a child only for an activity whose own start day is on or after the floor this run walks the feed from, so --since is one depth dimension over every Garmin fetch rather than one for the calendar series and an unbounded id-set difference for the three per-activity fetches. The bound lives in one function, garminPlanner.fanOutParents (internal/cli/garmin_plan.go), which both walkPerParent and the planner's seriesPerParent case call, so the estimate line, --dry-run, --status and the walk cannot disagree; --max-dependents stays what it was, a per-run safety valve over whatever remains in range. The docs say so before a run starts (decision D17): a first narrative recipe, "Before you run `history`", tells the reader where a fill starts, what it costs per request and per run, and how to see the estimate without paying for it.
reason: N131.4c. The N131 design (section 8, Q1) makes the local store a v1 requirement rather than a v2 line precisely because the 28-day figure is a page size and not a history limit: the reference account's steps reach 2020-07-06, 2 251 step-days, walked as 94 windows in 8.3 s. Section 9.1 recorded that the generated sync reports 'no temporal sync filters' for this API, and the press recon (N131.3 section 0.7) named the windowed backfill and its per-series day state as novel code from the outset. Every analytics recipe in Q2 -- sleep versus next-day performance, readiness honesty, rolling HRV and resting-HR baselines, zone distribution by season -- reads years of local rows, so none of them exists until this walk does.
validated_outcome: N131.5.2 (2026-09-13, builder round). gofmt -l clean over the tree, go vet ./... clean, go build ./... clean, go test -count=1 ./... green across 14 packages with 0 FAIL. TESTS FOR THE NEW MODEL: ascending order is proven from the fake client's request log for all three walked kinds (TestWalk_EveryKindRequestsOldestFirst) and again per kind (TestWalkWindowed_FullFillStartsAtTheHistoryFloorAndWalksOldestFirst starts at 2007-01-01; TestWalkPerDay_RequestsOnlySignalDaysOldestFirst asks for exactly the signal days and skips the calendar days between them; TestWalkActivities_PagesAscendingWithStartNotOffset asserts sortOrder=asc, start=0/100/200, no `offset` parameter and the probed floor as startDate). Depth: a deeper --since extends downward and re-requests nothing inside the filled range, a plain run makes exactly one catch-up call and leaves earliest_day alone, and a shallower --since neither shrinks the archive nor asks below its floor. Interruption: a windowed run killed mid-walk resumes with one call for the missing tail; a per-day run killed at its tenth day resumes with the refresh window plus the unfinished tail and re-asks nothing older; a killed feed run resumes at startDate = the bookmark day rather than the floor, and skips the floor probe. The refresh window is pinned to exactly the newest seven complete signal days by a spelled-out list. Fix 3: a 403 after a 200 on a series with no rows is stepped over with one window_denied warning and the bookmark passing above it; a 403 BEFORE any 200 counts toward the wall and moves nothing (five calls at a five-failure limit, both state days unset); an all-refused series stops with all_windows_refused and an unmoved bookmark; a 403 on a series that already holds rows is an ordinary failure. Surface: --days, --backfill and --empty-window-ceiling are unknown flags (exit 2, probed against the built binary); --since rejects anything that is neither `all` nor YYYY-MM-DD and names both forms; --help offers only --since and --status while all eight mechanism flags remain resolvable; --max-dependents defaults to 0. Reports: --status renders the table and --json, and a state row from the retired walk reports 'state predates this walk; re-walks once' with its range blanked rather than promising coverage the next run is about to go and fetch. The estimate is spelled-out arithmetic (150 requests -> 1.075 minutes, 9.00035 MB) and switches to the archive's own average at 30 rows. A windowed series that completes a run having stored nothing now reaches the shared series_returned_no_rows warning like every other kind (TestWalkSeries_AWindowedSeriesThatStoredNothingWarnsToo) -- the retired backward walk's own never-returned-data reporting used to short-circuit that check, and retiring it would otherwise have let six series walk 257 empty windows in silence. The catalog's cheap-before-expensive order, which is what makes the estimate land after the archive holds the days and ids it counts, is pinned by TestSeriesCatalog_CheapSeriesComeBeforeTheExpensiveOnes. MUTATION-CHECKED, seven of them, each reverted: halving the sleep_detail byte constant, 7 -> 3 on the refresh window, making atHistoryEdge always true, flipping the feed to sortOrder=desc, and dropping the filled-range guard from the per-day day selection, restoring walkSeries' early return for the windowed kind, and moving `steps` to the end of the catalog each failed exactly the test that claims the property. FIRST-HAND PROBES against the Kavita home with the built binary (read-only: --status and --dry-run open the archive and never construct a client): `history --status` lists all fifteen series with their row counts; `history --dry-run` plans 16 810 requests, about 2.0 h, up to 259 MB from the 2007 floor, printing no sync_start or sync_progress event, which is what 'no traffic' looks like. PRESS LEGS on this tree, all with GARMIN_HOME pointed at the Kavita home: verify 46/46 PASS, verify-skill 0 findings, scorecard 93/100 (equal to the pre-change baseline at ed92dbacf), dogfood WARN with the two permanent items (the generated successfulNoop helper and the unregistered `sync`), gosec 34 findings (equal to baseline). scorecard --live-check was NOT run: the press samples every research.json novel-feature example (internal/pipeline/live_check.go:841-887), and one of this CLI's two is `auth login`, a credential-producing login that must never run inside a delegated agent. The `history` example was changed to `history --since all --dry-run` so that leg is harmless whenever it is next run. NOT VALIDATED HERE: no live Garmin fetch was made by the builder; the fill, the kill-and-resume proof and the fix-3 field evidence are N131.5.2h's legs. N131.5.2 FIX ROUND (2026-09-13, after two independent audits). Four state-stamping defects fixed, each with a mutation-checked regression test: an extension leg whose every window Garmin refused no longer moves earliest_day (and a later run re-requests the refused range -- TestWalkWindowed_AnAllRefusedExtensionLegLeavesTheFloorAndIsRetriedLater); a legacy walk_version-0 range is dropped at read by garminResumableState rather than folded into the row this walk writes (TestWalkWindowed_ALegacyRangeIsNotRecertifiedAsThisWalksCoverage, TestGarminResumableState_DropsALegacyRangeAndKeepsACurrentOne); a per-day series with no signal day stamps nothing and plans no coverage (TestWalkPerDay_NoSignalDayStampsNothingAndLeavesLaterRunsFree); and a floor above the newest complete day -- --since <today> -- stamps no range and pins no depth (TestWalkWindowed_SinceTodayStampsNoRangeAndDoesNotPinTheDepth). The cost line now reads "About R requests, T, up to S MB -- after which the archive covers <day> to today.", with singular/plural and a self-contained duration phrase, because the old opening named a floor a caught-up run never approaches and could print "about under a minute" (TestEstimateLine_NamesTheCoverageItLeavesBehindAndCountsOneRequestSingular). --status renders a caught-up series as "up to date" rather than the permanent refresh-window count, and the feed's unknown count as "pages until the feed ends" rather than "variable" (TestStatusCell_ACaughtUpSeriesReadsUpToDateAndTheFeedNamesItsUnknown); the --dry-run REQUESTS column keeps integers, since the estimate line sums them. Re-run on this tree: gofmt -l clean, go vet ./... clean, go test -count=1 ./... green across 14 packages 0 FAIL, verify 46/46, verify-skill 0 findings, scorecard 93/100 (baseline), dogfood WARN with the two permanent items and a fixed point after one restore of the two known drifts, gosec 34 findings / 29 nosec (baseline). No live Garmin fetch was made in this round either. The same ceiling guard was carried to the activity feed's forward leg after the round's own probe found it stamping earliest_day = today under --since <today> while the bookmark clamped to yesterday (TestWalkActivities_SinceTodayStampsNoRangeAndDoesNotPinTheDepth, mutation-checked); all three walked kinds now stamp a range endpoint only from a day this run asked for and Garmin answered. N131.5.3 (2026-09-13, builder round, fan-outs bounded by the floor). gofmt -l clean over the tree, go vet ./... clean, go build ./... clean, go test -count=1 ./... green across 14 packages with 0 FAIL (run with GARMIN_HOME unset; exporting it fails three pre-existing platform tests on a tenant-artifact env conflict). New tests: the fan-out fetches only activities on or after a --since floor and leaves the older one outstanding; --since all fetches every stored parent including a row with no start day at all; a plain run bounds the fan-out at the feed's filled range; --max-dependents truncates the bounded set and the progress line reports the bounded remainder; the planner's outstanding count equals the walk's request count on one fixture (the drift guard between the two call sites); an unreadable parent day warns once with its count and is not fetched; a bounded-to-nothing fan-out does not claim an unproven zero; every fan-out's parent resource is written by a catalog series; and the new store reader keys each row's field by its id and omits a row that has no such field. Mutation-checked: inverting the floor comparison in fanOutParents reddens six of them, dropping the bound from the planner's seriesPerParent case only reddens the plan-vs-walk test, and fetching an unreadable-day parent blind reddens the warning test; all three reverted. Press legs on the Kavita home: verify 46/46 PASS (data-pipeline leg SKIP), verify-skill 0 findings, scorecard 93/100 Grade A (no --live-check), dogfood WARN with the two permanent items (successfulNoop, unregistered sync) and a fixed point across three renders, gosec 34 issues / 29 nosec (baseline). Read-only CLI probes on the Kavita home, no Garmin traffic: --status unchanged in shape, and both --dry-run plans read 0 outstanding for all three fan-outs on that drained archive, with the bound visible in the note as 2026-09-01 under --since and as the feed's earliest day 2011-10-29 on a plain run. Live leg (N131.5.3 d, 2026-09-13) on a sqlite3 .backup copy of the Kavita archive reached through --db with Kavita's credentials, the three children deleted in the copy for the 80 activities starting on or after 2026-08-01: --since 2026-09-01 fetched 28 children per fan-out (27 stored September activities plus one new 2026-09-13 activity the feed stored first in that run) and no child of any earlier activity, leaving the 53 August parents missing; a later --since 2026-08-01 fetched exactly those 53 per fan-out and re-fetched no September one (synced_at cohorts kept); a plain run fetched 0; --max-dependents 5 fetched 5 per fan-out with '23 pending' and three max_dependents_cap_hit warnings, and the uncapped re-run fetched the disjoint 23; the sync_estimate request counts (113, 188, 29, 44, 98) equalled the observed fan-out plus per-day requests in every run; zero 429/403/401. The real archive's 15 per-type counts were identical before and after (the CLI's learn subsystem opens the home archive on every invocation regardless of --db, so its file mtime moves; logical content does not).
regen_notes: FIXED HERE, AND A REPRINT REVERTS IT (N131.4g): the generated activity-feed paginator used cursorParam "offset", which Garmin ignores -- verified live 2026-09-07 -- so every walk was silently truncated to the newest page by the stuck_pagination guard. Three generated call sites now send the wire name `start`: internal/cli/sync.go determinePaginationDefaults case "activities", internal/cli/activities_list.go's resolvePaginatedReadWithStrategy call (which backs `activities list --all`), and internal/mcp/tools.go's mcpPageConfig for /activitylist-service/activities/search/activities. cursorType stays "offset": only the query key was wrong. The press restores "offset" on every reprint because its pagination detection reads the spec parameter's Name and never its wire name -- internal/openapi/parser.go detectPagination matches originalCase["offset"], and internal/profiler/profiler.go inferPaginationParamsFromEndpoint reads param.Name -- while the spec declares `name: offset` with `x-url-name: start`. x-pp-pagination is not an escape hatch at 4.32.0: parser.go readPaginationExtension accepts the single string value "none" and warns on anything else, so {type: offset, cursor_param: start} cannot be declared. Re-apply these three edits after every reprint, or move the tool to spec_format: internal where spec.Pagination is expressible. `history` was never affected; it sends `start` itself.

The spec declares no native User-Agent headers, so the generated client sends the press's own UA. N131.0 research section 4.2 found Garmin's 429 is User-Agent-gated rather than IP-gated. The live run above supplied the native UA pair through the home's config.toml [headers] block. Whether that belongs in the spec, in config defaults, or in the novel auth writer is an auth-surface decision, not a sync one.

The 45 MB the first 56-day run produced is dominated by sleep_detail (about 88 KB per night, re-measured 2026-09-13 over 90 archived nights) and daily_hr (about 13 KB per day). That is the measured basis for walking the per-day series over signal days only rather than over the calendar, and for printing the cost before the per-day leg starts.

WHAT A FULL FILL COSTS UNDER THE NEW MODEL (read from the Kavita archive 2026-09-13 with `history --dry-run`, no traffic): 831 windowed requests from the 2007 floor (257 x 3 at 28 days, 20 x 3 at 364), the feed's own pages, 7 004 fan-out requests and 8 974 per-day requests -- 16 810 in total, about two hours at the 300 ms default, up to 259 MB. The 2007 floor costs about 220 more windowed requests per account than a first-activity floor would, which is roughly 1.5 minutes, and it is what makes a fill gap-proof: the owner's account has a multi-year gap the retired 13-empty-window ceiling would have stopped at.

The live incremental path is exercised against the in-process fake (TestWalkWindowed_APlainRunKeepsTheStoredDepth, TestWalkActivities_ForwardLegResumesFromTheBookmarkDay, TestWalkPerDay_SecondRunReAsksOnlyTheNewestSevenSignalDays). The live legs of N131.5.2h are what prove it end to end on a populated archive.

WHY `history` SUPERSEDES THE GENERATED `sync`, AND A REPRINT REVERTS THE OVERRIDE (N131.5.1, decision D11; supersedes the coexistence note this entry used to carry): two verbs writing one archive was a confusing surface on every output the press produces -- CLI help, README, SKILL and the MCP mirror -- and it stored the same data twice. `history` now carries the three fetches only `sync` used to make (activity detail, splits, heart-rate-zone configuration), so nothing is reachable through `sync` that `history` does not cover. The generated internal/cli/sync.go is NOT edited: newSyncCmd still compiles and is simply never registered. internal/cli/root.go registers newGarminSyncStubCmd under the name `sync` instead -- one AddCommand line, recorded in its own patch .printing-press-patches/garmin-sync-superseded.json, which is the line to re-apply after a reprint. EVIDENCE THAT NOTHING WAS LOST WHEN THE THREE FETCHES MOVED (read 2026-09-13, `select resource_type, count(*) from resources group by 1` on both homes' archives): the owner home's data.db holds zero rows of any resource type (read by the orchestrator on 2026-09-13 and not re-read when this patch was written, because that home is off limits to the builder), and the Kavita home's, read first-hand, holds account 1, activities 3255, activity_hr_zones 655, daily_hr 90, daily_summary 90, intensity_minutes 1028, max_metrics 446, resting_hr 2260, sleep_detail 90, sleep_score 1679, sleep_stats 2015, steps 2260 -- zero rows under the generated sync's own resource names (activity_service_activity*, heart_rate*) in either home, so the new series names had nothing to migrate and nothing was orphaned. The 12 generated "run `garmin-pp-cli sync` first" hints and sync_hint.go are deliberately left alone: they now lead to the stub, which names `history`. The spec strip (dropping the 17 x-pp-syncable and 3 x-pp-sync-walker markers so a naive reprint emits the press's own no-op sync) is deferred to N131.7; until then a reprint re-emits a working generated sync and the override above is what makes it a dead end again.

ARCHIVE NAME, AND A REPRINT DOES NOT REVERT IT (N131.4h, findings F2 / TB-F11): the generated defaultDBPathInDir keeps its token-scoped naming and is left untouched. The novel resolver garminArchivePath overrides it for `history` and `insights` and pins `<data>/data.db` so the generated commands follow. Nothing in the spec expresses this: the scoping is unconditional in the press's helpers.go template. If a future press release stops scoping the archive by credential, garminArchivePath becomes a no-op that only migrates old homes and can be deleted -- check defaultDBPathInDir after any press upgrade.

THE FIFTH SERIES KIND (N131.5.1): seriesSingleDocument is one request answering for the whole account, with no date and no parent id. hr_zone_config (/biometric-service/heartRateZones) is its only member. Two mechanics it depends on: store.UpsertKeyedBatch skips any row whose document is not a JSON object (internal/store/garmin_series.go:201-205), so a bare-array response is wrapped under one key before storage; and the row id is a fixed literal rather than a date, so a re-run upserts the same row instead of growing a fake time series. activity_splits keeps its wrapper now that the shape is known: live 2026-09-13 the response is an object carrying activityId, lapDTOs and eventDTOs, which the store would accept unwrapped, but 1 000 rows are already archived wrapped and the wrapper keys the row without trusting a body field the spec declares only as a FreeFormObject. activity_detail is stored exactly as Garmin returns it: the generated dependent scopes that payload to $.activity for its typed table (internal/cli/sync.go:2231), which is a projection for one table's columns, and every sibling key it drops is a reason to fetch detail at all.

--max-dependents IS PER FAN-OUT SERIES, NOT PER RUN (N131.5.1): the cap is applied inside walkPerParent (internal/cli/garmin_sync.go:1444-1446), which now runs for activity_hr_zones, activity_detail and activity_splits, so the 500 default allows up to 1 500 dependent fetches in one run rather than 500. Measured live 2026-09-13: one run of the three new series made 1 001 calls in about seven minutes at the 300 ms pacing. Whether the cap should instead be shared across the three fan-outs is an open design question for the owner, not decided here.

FIRST RUN ON AN EXISTING ARCHIVE RE-WALKS THE CHEAP SERIES ONCE (N131.5.2): both homes' archives carry state rows written by the retired backward walk, and those rows are read as unfilled (walk_version 0 < 2). So the first run under this code re-walks the windowed series from the 2007 floor -- about 831 windows, roughly six minutes at the 300 ms pacing -- and re-pages the feed. Nothing is re-fetched that need not be: stored rows upsert in place, and a per-day day that already has a row is skipped. `resources` rows are never deleted by any of this. A ROW ALREADY RE-STAMPED AT walk_version 2 CANNOT BE REPAIRED BY READING IT (N131.5.2 fix round, finding A1): the first build of this change folded a legacy earliest_day forward into the walk_version-2 row it wrote, so such a row now claims a range no walk under this code requested. garminResumableState (internal/cli/garmin_sync.go) clears a legacy range at read, which stops the fold happening again, but it cannot tell a folded row from an honest one. Read first-hand 2026-09-13 with sqlite3 against both archives: the Kavita home's steps/resting_hr (2020-07-06), sleep_stats/max_metrics (2020-07-07), sleep_score (2021-09-18) and intensity_minutes (2007-01-01) carry such a range -- its live runs never asked below 2026-06-01 -- while the owner home's rows are honest, its first live run having walked --since all from 2007-01-01. Before the D14 fill, clear earliest_day, last_complete_day and walk_version on the Kavita rows (an owner-gated archive write) or run that home's fill with an explicit --since; otherwise a later deeper --since fetches only down to the claimed floor.

THE ACTIVITY FEED'S DATE BOUNDS ARE HONOURED (N131.5.2h, probed live 2026-09-13 on the Kavita home): sortOrder=asc was probed by the orchestrator on both homes; startDate/endDate were exercised by the live leg, where `history --since 2026-06-01` against an archive holding 3 255 activities paged only start=0 and start=100 and stopped at 186 rows. The forward leg passes startDate only; the extension leg passes both.

--since IS THE ONLY DEPTH CONTROL, AND A PLAIN RUN NEVER DEEPENS (N131.5.2, decision D15): `history` on a filled series keeps the stored floor. This differs from the plan's shorthand '--since all is the default': the default is `all` only on a series that has no filled range yet. Without that distinction an explicit --since all and a plain `history` would be indistinguishable, and 'a later plain history never changes depth' could not hold.

THE ESTIMATE'S PLACEMENT RESTS ON CATALOG ORDER (N131.5.2): it is printed at the first per-parent or per-day series, which only means 'after the cheap series have filled the archive it reads' while the windowed series and the activity feed stay ahead of them in garminSeriesCatalog(). Reordering the catalog would make a first run estimate from an empty archive and report almost nothing to do; TestSeriesCatalog_CheapSeriesComeBeforeTheExpensiveOnes is what stops that landing silently.

THE FAN-OUT BOUND, AS BUILT (N131.5.3, decision D16). The floor a fan-out uses is derived, never probed: --since DATE gives that day; a plain run gives the activity feed's stored earliest_day when the feed has a filled range at the current walk version; --since all, and a plain run on a feed with no filled range, give the zero day, which means unbounded -- every stored parent, with no filtering and no warning, so `--since all fetches all` stays literally true. The zero day is the honest answer for the unfilled-feed case because the feed's own floor is then the account's first activity, which no stored parent can predate. Order inside walkPerParent: bound, then MissingResourceIDs over the bounded ids, then truncate to --max-dependents; the progress line's "N pending" counts the bounded outstanding set and the max_dependents_cap_hit text is unchanged. The parent's day is read with store.ResourceIDJSONFieldValues(resource, "startTimeLocal") and parsed by the same dayFromValue the signal-day union uses, so a fan-out and the per-day walk can never disagree about when an activity happened; that reader was added rather than a day-carrying store query so ResourceIDsNewestFirst keeps deciding the order the cap truncates. A parent whose day cannot be parsed is treated as outside the bound -- not fetched, not marked done -- and named once per run with its count in a new sync_warning reason, parent_day_unreadable. A run whose floor leaves a fan-out nothing to ask for suppresses the series_returned_no_rows warning, whose two named causes (no such data, wrong request shape) are both false in that case. No new state: the three fan-out series still keep total_rows only, the bound is recomputed every run from the depth and the feed's saved range, and MissingResourceIDs is what makes a later deeper --since cost only the parents that were out of range before. --status leaves their FILLED FROM blank, as it did before, and their OUTSTANDING is the bounded missing count; --dry-run leaves the per-parent SINCE column blank on purpose -- that column feeds the estimate line's own minimum, which means how deep the archive ends up reaching, and a fan-out's floor is where its parents start -- and carries the bound in the NOTE instead ("one request per activity starting on or after <day> with no row yet").

"BEFORE YOU RUN `history`" (N131.5.3, decision D17), AND A REPRINT KEEPS IT ONLY THROUGH research.json. The text lives in the manuscript narrative as the FIRST entry of narrative.recipes (title "Before you run `history`", command `garmin-pp-cli history --dry-run`); dogfood renders narrative recipes under "## Recipes" as "### <title>" in BOTH README.md and SKILL.md, so one narrative edit yields the one heading in both files and a hand-inserted copy would be overwritten. The same is true of the Quick Start comments: they render from narrative.quickstart, and a hand edit to README's history comment was reverted by the next dogfood run before being moved into the manuscript. What IS hand-held in both files is the history paragraph under "## Commands" / "## Command Reference", which dogfood leaves alone and which now says the per-activity fetches cover the activities that start on or after the day the run starts from. Owner-facing prose never names "the floor": the recipe, both hand-held paragraphs and the cobra Long for `history` all say "the day the run starts from", and only code comments and the estimate note's own date carry the implementation term. Provenance for the numbers in that recipe, which the SKILL copy deliberately does not carry: 0.41 s per request and 7 177 requests in 49 min on the Kavita home, 1 114 requests in 411 s on the owner home, both 2026-09-13. Two press drops have to be re-applied after the last dogfood of any round: README's "Created by" byline, which dogfood strips, and research.json's trailing newline, which it eats.

internal/cli/activities_list.go: the Example is hand-set to `activities list --limit 1 --json` (the press renders a bare `activities list`), so the first example a harness runs is one bounded page; a reprint reverts it.

A reprint re-emits the press's novel-feature stubs internal/cli/{history,sql,insights,insights_sleep,insights_training}.go and their tests; delete them again — garmin_sync.go, garmin_sql.go and garmin_insights.go are the commands.
